zebralogic.title: Assign fixed‑position attributes immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue directly states that a specific attribute value belongs to a particular house number, assign that value to that house right away and remove it from all other houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a house number together with an attribute (e.g., "The German is in the first house").
zebralogic.example: Leaving a fixed‑position attribute unassigned and later placing it elsewhere, causing a contradiction.

zebralogic.title: Interpret adjacency and ordering clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: Handle spatial clues in three distinct ways: (a) "directly left/right of" – enforce immediate adjacency with the indicated direction; (b) "next to each other" – enforce adjacency but allow either order; (c) "somewhere left/right of" – enforce only a relative ordering without requiring adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing any clue that describes the relative positions of two attribute values.
zebralogic.example: Treating "next to each other" as a directed adjacency and fixing a direction that is not specified, leading to an impossible configuration.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says "N houses between X and Y", ensure that exactly N houses separate X and Y, i.e., |pos(X) – pos(Y)| = N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a specific number of houses between two items.
zebralogic.example: Counting the N houses as the distance itself and placing the items N houses apart instead of N + 1.

zebralogic.title: Bind equivalence clues to the same house
zebralogic.principle: If a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., "The German is Eric" or "The Swedish person is Peter"), place both values in the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue directly links two attributes.
zebralogic.example: Treating "The German is Eric" as two separate statements and assigning them to different houses.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say X is somewhere left/right of Y impose only an ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(X) > pos(Y)), without requiring adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the phrasing "somewhere left/right of".
zebralogic.example: Assuming X must be directly adjacent to Y when the clue only says X is somewhere left of Y.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue forbids an attribute from a specific house (e.g., "Peter is not in the fifth house"), eliminate that possibility from the domain of that attribute.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains a negative placement.
zebralogic.example: Leaving a prohibited value in a house, later causing a conflict with another clue.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses; after assigning a value, remove it from the candidate lists of the other houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Throughout the solving process, after any assignment.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same pet to two different houses, violating the one‑per‑category rule.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: When outputting the final solution, write each attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem statement, preserving capitalization and spelling.

zebralogic.title: Make forced assignments when only one candidate remains
zebralogic.principle: If after applying all constraints a house (or an attribute) has exactly one possible remaining value, assign it immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a domain reduces to a single option.
zebralogic.example: Leaving a single‑candidate value unassigned and later creating an inconsistency.

zebralogic.title: Disambiguate overlapping attribute values using clue context
zebralogic.principle: When a value appears in more than one attribute category (e.g., "cat" in both Animal and Pet), use cue words in the clue such as "pet", "owner", "keeps", "has", "aquarium", "enthusiast" to decide which category the clue refers to; never assume the same word always maps to the same category.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing a clue that mentions a value that exists in multiple categories.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "cat lover" as referring to the Pet category instead of the Animal category, causing adjacency constraints to be applied to the wrong attribute.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Off‑by‑one confusion: the clue means there are N houses separating the two items, not that they are N houses apart.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that "N houses between X and Y" translates to |pos(X) – pos(Y)| = N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Treating linked attributes as independent and placing them in different houses.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue equates two values, enforce that they occupy the same house.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: Forgetting that each value must appear exactly once in its category.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After any assignment, remove that value from the candidate sets of all other houses.

zebralogic.description: Altering attribute values (spelling/casing) instead of copying them verbatim
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Attempting to 'normalize' text leads to mismatches with the verifier.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute strings exactly as they appear in the problem, preserving case and spelling.

zebralogic.description: Treating 'next to each other' as a directed adjacency (assuming a specific order)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Assuming the first mentioned item is left of the second when the clue only states they are adjacent.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Interpret "next to each other" as undirected adjacency; allow either order unless another clue fixes the direction.

zebralogic.description: Confusing overlapping attribute values across categories (e.g., interpreting 'cat lover' as referring to the Pet category instead of the Animal category)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: When the same word exists in multiple attribute sets, the model defaults to one category without checking contextual cues.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Use clue‑specific keywords ("pet", "owner", "keeps", "has", "aquarium", "enthusiast", etc.) to decide which attribute category the word belongs to.
